title: The Miranda Hypothesis: How Hamilton Poisoned Persona Evals - Jacob E. Thomas, Results Gen
talk_summary: A measurement-methodology talk arguing that persona/role-play evals reward fluency and stylistic consistency while structurally missing the dominant failure (anachronistic compositing from culturally dominant representations in the training corpus). It proposes corpus-bounded, temporally anchored, expert-gated evaluation with a pre-registered rubric, and argues the persona should live in an inspectable context-window configuration rather than fine-tuned weights.

takeaways.technique: Rubric that refuses to reward fluency/voice as its own axis
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately drop 'rhetorical authenticity' as a scoring axis because a model can sound right while reasoning wrong; voice is a secondary indicator, never a criterion, and plain-but-faithful beats fluent-but-wrong.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A response that sounds like Lincoln but reasons unlikes him fails. No matter how fluent.

takeaways.technique: Pre-registration of eval instrument and directional predictions before collecting data
takeaways.what_they_do: Moments, conditions, questions, weighted rubric and predicted directions are locked and timestamped before any response is collected, so results can't be accused of cherry-picking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You cannot accuse a pre-registered instrument of cherry-picking because the instrument and the predictions were fixed before the data existed.

takeaways.technique: Domain-expert-authored gold set as a build-time gate, not runtime cost
takeaways.what_they_do: An expert writes diagnostic questions, a held-out gold set and weighted rubric once; that becomes a pipeline gate re-run whenever the base model changes, with automated metrics doing cheap first-pass flagging.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The expert does not sit at the loop of runtime. The expert builds the instrument

takeaways.technique: Persona/behavior as inspectable configuration, not fine-tuned weights
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue fine-tuning dissolves provenance and amplifies latent corpus bias un-auditably, while context-window anchoring keeps every input diffable, revertible and handable to an expert; cite clinical studies where general models beat specialized fine-tunes via catastrophic forgetting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Fine-tuning suppresses random distortion at the surface while amplifying it underneath.
takeaways.numbers: 2026 Nature Medicine: general frontier models outperformed dedicated specialized clinical AI across 12 clinics; biomedically fine-tuned models underperformed their base models

takeaways.technique: Fidelity requires a relation to a record an automated judge cannot see
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue an LLM-as-judge metric can only measure fluency/personality, not fidelity to a source record, because fidelity lives in the gap between output and archive; the judge must have the archive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It structurally cannot adjudicate fidelity because fidelity lives in the gap between the text and the archive, and the metric cannot see the archive.

takeaways.technique: Temporal/state anchoring: instantiate at a specific moment, not an averaged composite
takeaways.what_they_do: They fix a temporal anchor and bound reasoning to documents available at that moment, because models otherwise blend all eras into one salient composite.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The persona is instantiated at a specific moment. Knowledge and language that predated are out of bounds
